# Results — Study 611 (mREIT Carry)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **"mortgage
REITs pay 10-14%: leveraged MBS carry that is real income (and real drawdowns) — harvest the
dividend stream and the carry compounds"** — decomposed on the sector bellwether **REM**
(iShares Mortgage Real Estate ETF, 2007→) plus the two flagship agency mREITs **NLY** and
**AGNC**, against a **duration-matched levered-IEF benchmark** (excess-on-excess, Newey-West
HAC). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is
dropped). Fingerprint `3b2ec2fc7dd3`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes, downloaded **twice**: auto-adjusted (**total-return**) and raw split-adjusted (**price-only**) — the monthly difference isolates the **dividend return** |
| Tickers | REM (sector ETF, the headline), NLY, AGNC (flagship agency mREITs), IEF (7-10y Treasuries, the duration), SPY (equity), BIL (1-3m T-bills, the cash/financing proxy) |
| Window | REM/NLY: 2007-06-30 → 2026-06-30 (**229 months**, 19.1 yrs — GFC included); AGNC: 2008-06 → 2026-06 (217 months) |
| Inference | Newey-West HAC *t* (6 lags; 3/12 as robustness) on the dividend component and on the factor-model alpha; Sharpe races are **excess-vs-excess** over BIL |
| Execution / costs | passive buy-and-hold decomposition — entry at the first month-end close of the window (the one documented lag; there is no timing signal). Two one-way ETF trades over 19.1 yrs at 5 bps ≈ **0.5 bps/yr** amortised; REM's 0.48%/yr expense ratio is inside the tape |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** REM is an index **fund** — its tape already
> contains every mortgage REIT that blew up inside the index (Thornburg, IndyMac-era casualties,
> the 2020 margin-call cohort), so the headline leg is **not** survivor-biased. The two single
> names NLY and AGNC **are** survivors — the two biggest agency mREITs still standing — and are
> quoted as colour, never as the headline: the honest sector number is REM's.

## The carry — the dividend stream is real (and enormous)

Monthly **dividend component** = total-return minus price-only return, per name (HAC *t*, 6 lags):

| name | window | dividend (bps/mo) | dividend (%/yr) | HAC *t* | TR CAGR | price-only CAGR | $100 → TR / price-only |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **REM** | 2007-06 → 2026-06 (n=229) | **+84.69** | **+10.65%** | **+18.09** | **−1.13%** | **−10.96%** | **$80.5 / $10.9** |
| NLY | 2007-06 → 2026-06 (n=229) | +103.04 | +13.09% | +23.01 | +7.52% | −5.18% | $399.0 / $36.2 |
| AGNC | 2008-06 → 2026-06 (n=217) | +121.46 | +15.59% | +17.80 | +11.80% | −3.22% | $751.4 / $55.3 |

The **10-14% coupon is real**: the harvested dividend stream is +10.65%/yr on the sector fund
(HAC *t* = **18.09**) and 13-16%/yr on the flagships — exactly the pitch. And it was **fully
consumed by NAV erosion** on the sector: REM's price leg fell **−10.96%/yr**, leaving a
**negative** total-return CAGR (−1.13%/yr) over 19.1 years. $100 harvested ~10.65%/yr of
"income" the whole way down to **$80.5**.

## Risk & return — the sector fund vs its ingredients (REM window, monthly TR)

| | CAGR | vol | Sharpe (excess over BIL) | max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **REM** | **−1.13%/yr** | 24.17% | **+0.04** | **−67.44%** |
| IEF | +3.32%/yr | 6.70% | +0.32 | −23.15% |
| SPY | +10.68%/yr | 15.58% | +0.64 | −50.78% |
| BIL | +1.36%/yr | 0.56% | — | −0.42% |

REM's excess return over bills is **+7.78 bps/mo at HAC *t* = +0.18** — over 19 years the
levered-MBS-carry vehicle is statistically **indistinguishable from cash**, at 24% vol and a
−67% drawdown. Equity vol, T-bill return.

## Carry premium vs the duration-matched benchmark (the decisive test)

Newey-West (6 lags) regression of each name's monthly **excess** return on IEF and SPY
**excess** returns — the passive levered-Treasuries-plus-equity-beta mix an investor could hold
instead of the packaged carry. The betas are full-sample (a benchmarking choice for a risk
decomposition, stated openly — nothing here is a timed trading rule):

| name | alpha (bps/mo) | alpha (%/yr) | **HAC *t*** | β_IEF (t) | β_SPY (t) | R² | CAGR vs bench | maxDD vs bench |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **REM** | **−87.62** | **−10.02%** | **−2.50** | +0.42 (+1.91) | +1.05 (+6.80) | 0.46 | −1.13% vs **+12.07%** | −67.4% vs −49.7% |
| NLY | −8.11 | −0.97% | −0.22 | +1.05 (+4.06) | +0.78 (+4.34) | 0.31 | +7.52% vs +11.03% | −45.8% vs −33.4% |
| AGNC | +18.83 | +2.28% | +0.43 | +1.20 (+4.41) | +0.82 (+5.03) | 0.32 | +11.80% vs +12.03% | −48.1% vs −36.0% |

Two findings. **(1) The costume comes off:** REM's SPY beta is **+1.05** (*t* = 6.80) against a
duration beta of just +0.42 — the "bond-like carry" vehicle is *equity* risk, not levered
Treasuries. **(2) The packaged carry destroys value vs DIY:** REM's alpha versus its own
beta-matched benchmark is **−87.62 bps/mo (−10.02%/yr) at HAC *t* = −2.50** — a *significantly
negative* carry premium (mean-spread HAC *t* = −3.01). Even the two surviving flagships add
nothing over their benchmark (*t* = −0.22 and +0.43) while carrying 12-14 pp deeper drawdowns.

## Robustness — the negative alpha is not a lag-choice or GFC artefact

| variant | REM alpha (bps/mo) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| NW lags = 3 | −87.62 | −2.32 |
| **NW lags = 6 (headline)** | **−87.62** | **−2.50** |
| NW lags = 12 | −87.62 | −2.78 |
| ex-GFC subperiod (2010-01 →) | −76.48 | −1.93 |

Ex-GFC the alpha is still −76 bps/mo (*t* = −1.93, marginal on the shorter tape) with the
dividend stream intact (+10.33%/yr, *t* = 17.0) and the price leg still eroding (−5.78%/yr,
TR +4.28%/yr vs the benchmark's double digits). The erosion is chronic, not one crisis.

## Crisis autopsies — "real drawdowns" is the honest half of the pitch

Peak-to-trough **total-return** drawdowns inside each fixed, documented window (daily tape):

| crisis | REM | NLY | AGNC | SPY | IEF |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GFC 2007-09 | **−74.7%** | −40.9% | −31.0%* | −55.2% | −6.2% |
| Taper tantrum 2013 | −24.8% | −34.6% | −36.9% | −5.6% | −9.1% |
| COVID 2020 | **−68.5%** | −60.1% | −51.8% | −33.7% | −4.7% |
| Rate shock 2022 | −40.3% | −47.8% | −48.2% | −24.5% | −17.4% |

*\*AGNC listed 2008-05; its GFC cell covers only the tail of the crisis.*

In every stress the "income sleeve" fell **more than the stock market** — including −68.5% in
*eight weeks* in 2020 (the repo margin spiral) while the duration it supposedly monetises (IEF)
*rose*. mREIT leverage is short-funded (repo) and convexity-hedged, so the carry is short
liquidity and short volatility: crises are when the financing disappears.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is faithful

Deterministic three-factor world with a **planted** mean carry and a **planted** benchmark
alpha (seed 611; payout jitter keeps the detector test non-degenerate):

| planted | dividend detector | alpha test | betas recovered |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| carry = 0, alpha = 0 (null) | +1.49 bps/mo (*t* = +0.71) | −6.45 bps/mo (*t* = −0.35) | 2.64 / 0.56 |
| carry = +100 bps/mo, alpha = −70 bps/mo | +101.49 bps/mo (*t* = +48.21) | −76.45 bps/mo (*t* = −4.15) | 2.64 / 0.56 (planted 2.50 / 0.55) |

Under the null neither detector manufactures significance; planted values are recovered.
*(A faithful-engine check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamps.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The leveraged-MBS carry *exists* and is huge: the sector fund harvested
  **+84.69 bps/mo (+10.65%/yr)** of pure dividend return at **HAC *t* = +18.09** (NLY 13.09%/yr
  at *t* = 23.01, AGNC 15.59%/yr at *t* = 17.80) — and the erosion financing it is just as
  real: REM's carry premium vs its duration-matched benchmark is **−87.62 bps/mo at HAC
  *t* = −2.50**, robust across HAC lags. The claim's numbers (10-14% paid, real drawdowns) are
  on the tape. Survivorship: the headline leg (REM) is an index fund, not survivor-biased; the
  single names are survivors and quoted as colour.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** 19.1 years of harvesting a 10.65%/yr coupon left $100 at **$80.5**
  (TR CAGR **−1.13%/yr**, excess over bills *t* = +0.18 — cash, statistically) at **24% vol**
  and a **−67% drawdown**, losing **−10.02%/yr (HAC *t* = −2.50)** to a passive levered
  IEF+SPY mix anyone could hold. A worse bond, a worse stock, and a worse *carry trade* than
  DIY. Costs are not the issue (~0.5 bps/yr amortised); the vehicle is.
- **"10-14% free lunch (income you can spend without touching capital)"? — BUSTED.** The
  coupon is fully financed by NAV erosion: REM's price leg fell **−10.96%/yr** ($100 → $10.9
  price-only). Spend the dividend and you are spending your own principal — with an equity
  beta of 1.05 and a repo margin call attached.
